author: reek
body: `show` on a unit type must answer the value, not the machine representation of it. `emit-show-builtin` dispatches on the operand type, and until 2026-07-28 it dispatched on the WRAPPER: a unit type missed the arm its inner type is entitled to and fell to the `otherwise` arm, which is `__itoa`. A unit Text printed 1132612 (the pointer), a unit Boolean printed 1 (the raw tag), and a unit Real printed 4612811918334230528, which is 0x4004000000000000 -- 2.5 as an IEEE double, rendered as a decimal integer. Measured on seed 759D3E0F and again, byte-identically, on 6ED0A257.

author: reek
body: Every row is asked twice, unwrapped and wrapped, and the unwrapped answer is the control. A row means nothing on its own: `show` could be broken for Text outright and the wrapped row would still differ from the value. It is the two columns AGREEING that says the wrapper was seen through.

author: reek
body: The Integer rows are why this was cheap to miss and are kept for that reason. `otherwise` is the CORRECT destination for a unit Integer, so that row was right before the fix and is right after it. A spot check that reached for the obvious unit type would have found nothing wrong.
